nodes.name: Daily Schedule
nodes.notes: Starts the workflow on a timer — daily at 7:00. No input data; downstream nodes fetch what they need.

nodes.name: Map to Canonical Schema
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes jobId, kind, payload. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Route by Event Kind
nodes.notes: Routes each item to one of 3 lanes: job.start, job.done + fallback. Watch out: Unmatched items go to the fallback output; without one they are silently dropped.

nodes.name: Handle 'job.start' → Google Sheets
nodes.notes: Upserts a row into 'Job Tracker', matched on jobId — re-running with the same key updates the row instead of duplicating it. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Handle 'job.done' → Forward API
nodes.notes: POST https://api.example.com/v1/jobs — retries 3× with backoff on failure. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: API key / bearer for the target API. Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.

nodes.name: Log Unrecognized Kind
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Job Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Consolidate Handling
nodes.notes: Rejoins 3 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build a stable idempotency key per job (djb2 hash, no deps) Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Drop Already-Processed Items
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.name: Load Previous Snapshot
nodes.notes: Reads every row from 'Job Tracker' — the read side of the store, e.g. for a digest or a downstream sync. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Compute Drift vs Snapshot
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Compare current metrics with the previous snapshot Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Enrich with Reference Data
nodes.notes: GET https://enrichment.example.com/v2/lookup — retries 3× with backoff on failure. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: API key / bearer for the target API. Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.

nodes.name: Fold In Enrichment Fields
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes enrichedAt, enrichmentSource. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Stamp Completion Time
nodes.notes: Stamps completedAt with the current time for auditing.

nodes.name: Persist Run Metadata
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Serialize Run Output (CSV)
nodes.notes: Serializes items to a CSV binary file.

nodes.name: Archive Row Snapshot
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Job Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
nodes.notes: Delegates to a reusable sub-workflow (single-responsibility building block) and waits for its result. Watch out: The sub-workflow needs an Execute Sub-workflow Trigger as its entry point. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run.

nodes.name: Record Sub-workflow Result
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Stamp Processing Time
nodes.notes: Stamps processedAt with the current time for auditing.

nodes.name: Cap Batch Volume
nodes.notes: Caps the stream at 50 items to protect downstream quotas.

nodes.name: Align Field Names
nodes.notes: Normalizes field names so every source feeds the same downstream schema.

nodes.name: Guard Non-Empty type
nodes.notes: Drops items that fail the condition; only qualifying items continue (no false branch).

nodes.name: Sort Jobs Newest First
nodes.notes: Orders items (newest first) so limits and digests pick the most relevant records.

nodes.name: Save Execution Metadata
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Summarize Run Stats
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes runAt, itemCount, status. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

# Orchestrate a routine task on a schedule

**Pattern:** Workflow Automation · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers process-orchestration work end to end across Google Sheets and Slack.

It moves through 28 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Daily Schedule
2. Map to Canonical Schema
3. Route by Event Kind
4. Handle 'job.start' → Google Sheets
5. Handle 'job.done' → Forward API
6. Log Unrecognized Kind
7. Consolidate Handling
8. Fingerprint for Idempotency
9. Drop Already-Processed Items
10. Load Previous Snapshot
11. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
12. Enrich with Reference Data
13. Fold In Enrichment Fields
14. Stamp Completion Time
15. Persist Run Metadata
16. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
17. Archive Row Snapshot
18. Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
19. Record Sub-workflow Result
20. Stamp Processing Time
21. Cap Batch Volume
22. Align Field Names
23. Guard Non-Empty type
24. Sort Jobs Newest First
25. Save Execution Metadata
26. Summarize Run Stats
27. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
28. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing process-orchestration work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Daily Schedule → Map to Canonical Schema → Route by Event Kind → Handle 'job.start' → Google Sheets → Handle 'job.done' → Forward API → Log Unrecognized Kind → Consolidate Handling → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow → Record Sub-workflow Result → Stamp Processing Time → Cap Batch Volume → Align Field Names → Guard Non-Empty type → Sort Jobs Newest First → Save Execution Metadata → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and Slack aligned by hand for process orchestration
- Process orchestration work where "Map to Canonical Schema" is still a manual step before Google Sheets
- Process orchestration work that only reaches Google Sheets on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and Slack in step for process orchestration, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Google Sheets or Slack are skipped, across all 31 nodes of this process-orchestration build
- A failed Google Sheets or Slack call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 31 nodes in this process-orchestration build
- Branches rejoin before Google Sheets, so a process-orchestration run reports once rather than 31 times
- Every process-orchestration run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Google Sheets

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Google OAuth2 / service account; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

The optional HMAC check runs before any business logic touches the payload — bad signatures are rejected at the door rather than after work has already been done with untrusted data. Acking fast (HTTP 202) and doing the real work after the response is what stops the sender's webhook delivery from timing out and re-delivering the same event.

## Practice exercises

About as deep as this pattern goes — extend it:

1. Turn on signature verification and trace what a tampered payload does at the 'Signature Valid?' gate.
2. Add a new event kind to the switch and give it its own handler.
3. Remove the fast-ack step and observe how response time changes under a slow downstream write.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your process orchestration process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole process-orchestration payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
